exclude: Exact copy of BASIC ROM 901226-01 offsets $0000–$015F in both the entry and play snapshots

comments.text: The menu writes one to the KERNAL keyboard buffer capacity at $804A before it begins polling.
The music player saves this vector and installs $5B18 when it starts from idle. It restores the caller's processor-port setting after installing the handler.
High byte of the KERNAL IRQ vector. The song player saves it to its chained jump operand before installing its own handler.
Color-cell bytes paired with the active bitmap. VIC bank zero and the screen offset in D018 select this page.
The menu color write at $835A uses a patched operand here. In the play snapshot the last selected destination row starts at this address.
The scene blitter writes a color nibble pair through this operand, updated from the destination row table.
Retained BASIC start wrapper at $0801. Its second line calls SYS 16384 and has a trailing crack attribution.
First byte of the game state cleared at $400F. The path at $4609 tests its low four bits to choose a behavior.
Initialized to 50 at $401A. The main loop counts it down toward zero at $4098, using $0908 as a prescaler.
Starts at 200 and reloads to 200 each time it counts through zero in the main loop.
Starts at 14. The main loop redraws and decrements it after each 150 passes, and sets the game-state byte to 2 when the meter reaches zero.
The heart pickup at $5601 increments this count before adding item $10 to the inventory.
Starts at 25. Heart pickup decrements this and redraws the two digits at $81E9. End-of-game processing also writes it at $819A.
Starts at one for the spinach. Pickup tests it against eight, and removal at $50F9 decrements it.
Incremented by the main loop. The love meter update and reset start when it reaches 150.
Starting room 5. The transition code writes the destination index here. The room renderer compares it with $40D8 before rebuilding its static layers.
Cleared at the beginning of a pass. The input reader overwrites it when the combined keyboard and joystick mask is nonzero, preserving the last nonzero mask across later polls in that pass.
Eight item slots. Zero denotes an empty slot. The high nibble selects the HUD drawing stream at $81FA.
Accumulates the action masks from the five matrix tests in $4DC7. The joystick direction bits are merged afterward.

Dispatches effect index A through the table at $0A92, unless $FFF6 blocks it. Special entries include $FE, which queues a change at the next control poll, and $FD, which reads oscillator 3 bit zero to choose one of two effects.
Looks up a voice slot from the effect's first byte at $FD29, clears its state, then loads fields from the pointer at $18/$19 into that voice's work record.
Clears the five per-channel bytes indexed by $FD29 and clears the gate-state byte in the mapped hardware voice slot.
Saves processor flags and masks interrupts while refreshing effect voices through $0C57, then restores flags.
Clears $FD33 and scans three voice slots through the offset table at $0A0D to refresh sound state.
Tests the current voice's two-byte duration. At zero resets channel state and advances the event index, either ending the voice or decoding the next event.
Looks up the current voice event through $0B4C, then copies the first two bytes to the duration fields and decodes control and filter bits from the following byte.
Marks a slot relative to $FD29 active, then reads timing and parameter bytes through the current stream pointer.
Maps the channel to a work slot, tests the active byte, advances the timing count and fetches the next stream byte when its period expires.
Writes packed filter cutoff, resonance and routing and mode/volume values from the instrument state under KERNAL ROM to the active SID registers.
Loads frequency, pulse width, ADSR and control from the work area indexed by X. Y is the SID voice register offset.
Split low and high bytes of scenery drawing pointers. The renderer masks object ID bit 7 before indexing, and uses that bit to select the pass that draws the object.
Most significant byte array paired with $1000. Both scenery passes load it into $8D after masking the cell's high bit.
Scene drawing commands for map ID $31 from the split pointer table at $1000. Starts by dispatching scenery subcommand $06.
Scene drawing commands for map ID $32 from the split pointer table at $1000. Starts by dispatching scenery subcommand $07.

Scene drawing commands for map ID $09 from the split pointer table at $1000. Shifts the draw position by row delta $02 and column delta $FF.

Scene drawing commands for map ID $2C from the split pointer table at $1000. Contains sound command $09 before processing any drawing cells.

Scene drawing commands for map ID $26 from the split pointer table at $1000. Starts by dispatching scenery subcommand $01.
Drawing stream for actor shape index $06 in the split table read at $4262 and $4267. Calls substream $1F43 before processing its following commands.
Drawing stream for actor shape index $07 in the split table read at $4262 and $4267. Calls substream $BC20 before processing its following commands.
Drawing stream for actor shape index $08 in the split table read at $4262 and $4267. Calls substream $BC6C before processing its following commands.
Drawing stream for actor shape index $03 in the split table read at $4262 and $4267. Calls substream $BDEC before processing its following commands.
Drawing stream for actor shape index $04 in the split table read at $4262 and $4267. Calls substream $BE56 before processing its following commands.
Drawing stream for actor shape index $05 in the split table read at $4262 and $4267. Calls substream $BE9C before processing its following commands.
Operand target of the menu glyph copier at $8362 in the play snapshot. The destination changes with UI row and column.
Calls machine setup at $4BE5 and jumps to game-state initialization at $400F.
Clears $46 bytes of game state, sets room 5, the 25-heart counter, the starting spinach and life meter, then runs the menu and initializes the resident room tables and sound.
Runs a gameplay pass with buffer page $6C, checks the game-state flag, updates the score bonus prescaler, and counts down the love meter every 150 passes.
Clears the input latch, prepares the room buffers, polls controls, runs the intervening $4E79 update and polls again before advancing object scripts.
After the second control poll, transfers to the actor script dispatcher with a tail jump.
Initialized to $FF so the first gameplay pass takes the room rebuild branch. Compared with and updated from $0925.
Rebuilds the static room cache on a room-index change. Clears the foreground mask bit in cached triples and draws depth layers 0 through 2, interleaving input polls.
Uses the room index to choose a four-by-four window in a page group. Draws nonzero scenery entries with bit 7 clear using the split pointers at $1000 and $1038.
For a selected depth layer, draws scenery entries whose high bit is set and draws the eligible item classes from the high nibble of the adjacent map plane. Skips zero and item class seven.
Visits a six-by-six window around the room grid. Every set bit in its fourth plane selects an actor slot. The slot's shape index and cell-relative offsets select a stream and its draw position.
Copies the current cell coordinates into the stream renderer's coordinates before falling through.
Initializes drawing state and walks the stream at $8C/$8D. Values from $F0 up dispatch through the split command table using an indirect jump.
Split pointers indexed by drawing command $F0 through $FF at $42EE and $42F3.
Handles stream bytes below $F0 on the rendering path. The first bounds check tests the row coordinate in $8E against 24.
Clears the temporary drawing mode and restores saved Y before returning. Shared by drawing opcodes $F0, $F1, $F2 and $FF.
Adds the next two bytes to row and column respectively and continues at the next command.
Saves the stream pointer, draws from the little-endian target, restores the caller's stream pointer and skips the pointer bytes.
Takes the next two bytes as the replacement stream pointer and resumes decoding without saving the old stream.
Reads a count into $0926, advances the pointer and patches the repeat command with the restart position.
Decrements the repeat counter. Resumes at the saved position if it remains nonzero, otherwise continues from the current pointer.
Loads a stream parameter into $0928, which changes how the cell decoder obtains a component of each entry.
Loads the next stream byte into $0927. The cell decoder stores it at offset zero of the destination triple.
Increments the counter byte in the current stream, compares it against two thresholds and either skips the five-byte operand, resets and skips it, or transfers through the embedded pointer.
Uses a four-bit random value with rejection to index a list after the command, then writes the chosen value into the stream and continues there.
Uses a four-bit random value with rejection to choose one of the little-endian pointers after the command.
Reads an effect number from the drawing stream. Effects 2 and 3 are requested in rooms 0 and 1, while other numbers bypass that room test.
Reads a subcommand from the current drawing stream and jumps through the low and high handler bytes relative to $45CB and $45D7.
Tests bit 3 of $0903 and chooses between streams $1141 and $1156 before jumping to the renderer.
When bit 1 of $0935 is set, advances $0922 and selects alternate drawing streams on counts 7, 15 and 23, with a separate update at count 23. The counter rolls over at 60.
Returns $48DF on every third call, with zeros between, via the counter at $48DE.
Builds static scenery in three passes using RAM with I/O hidden. The layer-one and layer-two passes split interleaved scratch-buffer triples into separate pages for later compositing.
Adds three to the scratch pointer at $B0/$B1 and propagates carry into the high byte.
Walks eligible rectangle bounds from $7544 and related tables, scanning the chosen scenery-cache plane and setting bit 6 on nonzero cells that have not already been marked.
Generates the low and high bytes of three times the index in pages $7E and $7F for the interleaved draw buffer.
Clears nine pages beginning at $6C00 with all 256 offsets in each page visited in descending order from zero.
Copies nine pages from physical RAM $D000–$D8FF to $6C00–$74FF.
Zeros twelve pages at $6000–$6BFF. The room placement stream fills these planes later in start-up.
Increments the low nibble of Y within a 16-column row. From column 15 wraps to zero while preserving the row.
Decrements the low nibble of Y within a row. At column zero ORs in $0F to wrap to the last column.
Adds $10 to Y, moving down one row of the 16-column grid.
Subtracts $10 from Y, moving up one row of the 16-column grid.

Stops the preceding sound state, sets CIA interrupt routing, copies eight RAM vector bytes and configures the keyboard directions and timer registers. Enables bitmap mode before clearing and initializing the display.
Clears $2000 through $3FFF and $0400 through $07FF before drawing begins.
Builds the split table for eight times the glyph index at $C800 and $C900, then reverses the eight bits of each index into $CA00.
Updates the four-byte state at $4D9F with shifts, addition and carry propagation. Returns its new low byte in A and restores X.
Five CIA port-A row values for the remappable action keys. The scan pairs these with masks at $4DBD and action bits at $4DC2.
Five active-low column masks for the selected rows. A zero AND result means the corresponding key is down.
Five bits ORed into $0940 for successful matrix tests.

Temporarily sets the processor port to $35 for I/O. Scans five keys, merges active-low joystick direction bits from CIA1 port A, advances sound, restores Y and the banking byte, and returns the latched control mask.

Saves A and the banking value, enables I/O and acknowledges CIA1. If the Timer B status bit is set, preserves X and Y around the indirect handler call before restoring banking and returning from interrupt.
Jumps indirectly through the RAM vector at $FFF8. The timer IRQ reaches this with a JSR, so its handler can return to $4E65.
Four little-endian addresses copied to physical RAM $FFF8–$FFFF by $4BE5. The first is the initial sound callback, followed by NMI, reset and IRQ.

Walks the active rectangle bounds, derives row and byte addresses from coordinate tables, then examines cell triples in the render buffer. Marks visited triples with bit 6 before taking the bitmap write path.
The cell's first byte replaces the bank immediate operand at $4F47 before the tile row address is computed.

Loads the cell ID and draw flags from the interleaved buffer. Uses the tile bitmap base table, writes its screen color byte and copies the eight bitmap rows, reversing the bits on the signed-cell path.
Maps the six-bit cell color selector to the VIC bitmap screen byte. Used on both the plain-color and tile-copy paths.

Reads the resident stream at $C000. FF FD selects a room origin, FF FE selects a depth group, FF FC supplies a slot index. Other five-byte records place four plane values at a cell offset. The stream ends at FF FF.
For each set bit in the fourth plane's new cell value, records Y and the plane page in the matching 12-byte actor slot.
Writes Y and the third plane's page number as a two-byte pair at $0909 plus twice A.
Pre-increments the absolute operand of its own LDA, then reads the next byte. The installer initializes the operand to $BFFF so the first read is $C000.
Sets four zero-page pointers to consecutive pages for depth 0, 1 or 2. Groups begin at $6000, $6400 and $6800.
Maps sixteen room indices to offsets within a 16-by-16 plane. Its four groups start at offsets 0, $40, $80 and $C0.
Scans for a zero slot and writes A there, then redraws the inventory. The pickup path checks capacity before calling it.
Finds the first slot equal to A, shifts following bytes one place toward it through destination slot seven, decrements the inventory count and redraws. Returns early if no slot matches.
Copies 18 bytes from $5151 to $5163 at game start.
Saves the descriptor pointer from A and Y. Tests scene state and actor occupancy one grid row down, then selects the drawing stream from the descriptor and the surrounding state.
Checks $0903 state bits and the six three-byte symbol records. If the target matches, jumps to $5296. Otherwise, on the reroll path, draws six random values from 5 through 14.
Six target bytes compared with the first byte of each three-byte record at $5163.
Compares the target table with six live symbols at stride three and returns Z set when all match.
Requests sound six times, sets bit 5 of $0903, and sets six item-plane cells in page $65 to heart code $10.
Eight records of twelve bytes. The first word is the script position, and the next pair selects the cell in the actor mask planes.
Last byte in an actor slot, used as an offset in the actor rectangle computation at $5ECD.
Copies 96 initial bytes from $59F9 to $52CD, for eight 12-byte slots.
Walks the slot index table at $535A, dispatching the corresponding actor scripts through $5361. A zero slot index ends the traversal with a tail call.
Copies a 12-byte slot to zero page. Advances its two-byte stream pointer and uses the second byte of a command pair to select a handler when the pair's OR equals $3F and is nonzero.

Looks three pages behind the actor's cell pointer for linked tile types 5 and 6. For type 6 saves the room and cell, installs the stored start-side position, and sets room 5. Type 5 looks up the saved room.

Takes the latched mask, tests direction bits in priority order and adds a direction selector from one to four to the script pointer. The hold path clears and polls the latch until one of the four direction bits is present.
Takes a nonzero byte below or above $3F as an index into the actor's pointer table, then loads that address. Zero and $3F return without changing the pointer.

Tests two candidate cells, branches for class-seven items, and rejects normal pickup at eight slots. Otherwise increments the count, requests sound and clears the item in the plane. Heart pickup updates both the held-heart and remaining-heart counters.
Temporarily subtracts two pages from the actor's plane address, reads the item byte at the same cell then restores the page. Returns Z set if the item byte is zero.
Inspects bit 5 in the adjoining plane when the depth byte at $0934 permits the direction, then selects the normal or alternate script continuation.
Uses the other neighboring plane, four pages from the lower-plane address, and shares the bit-5 test at $567D.

Checks the actor depth before selecting the adjacent plane. If the cell's flag bit 5 is set and its scenery code is $81 or $82, checks inventory class three against the cell coordinates linked to each key.
Decrements the cell column and begins the room-index update when a leftward move crosses a four-column room boundary.
Decrements the current room index when the leftward move crosses a four-column room boundary, then falls through the shared store.
Writes the destination room index in A. The following movement code records the destination cell and sets its actor bit.
Clears the old actor bit and adds 16 to the cell index. When that crosses a four-row room boundary, updates the room index before recording the new cell.
Interleaved pointers for actor-script commands starting at index one. The dispatcher at $53BE doubles the command index before loading the low and high bytes at $598A and $598B.
Source of eight 12-byte records copied into active slots at $52CD. The eighth record starts with all fields clear.
Selects parameter set Y and writes the envelope and pulse values to a SID voice register group computed from A. Temporarily exposes the I/O area and restores the prior processor-port value.

Enables the requested voice slots from the low three bits in A, initializes their stream pointers and first events, and installs sound callbacks in the hardware-RAM and KERNAL IRQ paths when the player was idle.
Reads the CIA1 interrupt register and invokes the sound tick on Timer B. Continues through the saved KERNAL interrupt-vector destination.
Calls the sound tick at $5B2B, then jumps through a patched target for the prior RAM handler.
High byte of the saved RAM callback address in the jump operand at $5B28.

When active, counts five timer interrupts before updating the three voices. Handles delayed gate changes, reads new events when a voice duration expires, and takes the shutdown path when the stop flag is set.
Writes the three cached control bytes at $5D0B–$5D0D to SID voices one through three.
Loads CIA1 Timer B with low byte $FF and high byte from $5D23, enables its interrupt source and starts it with a forced reload.
Takes the voice slot in X, fetches its next stream event and updates duration and pitch. Bit 6 disables the slot, and a negative event or the last voice ending takes a carry-set exit.
Clears the sequencer flag, writes the idle voice controls with I/O visible, restores the prior vectors and timer values if playing, and then restores processor flags and banking.
Restores CIA1 Timer B latch and the original hardware-RAM and KERNAL IRQ callback addresses saved at song start.

Scans the four-by-four room window through the depth groups. Selected item classes contribute rectangle bounds in the tables at $7544, $7561, $757E and $759B. A room-index vector chooses the next routine.
Room-five callback selected by the table at $7500. Reads the state bits and conditionally queues drawing or sound actions.
Sets the initial rectangle count to $12, gathers room foreground rectangles, then computes actor rectangle bounds.
Finds the corner of the expanded room window. Walks the eight actor slots at stride twelve and combines their current cell indices, offsets and shape bounds to update the dirty rectangles.
Loads the actor shape index from its live slot through an operand patched by the preceding instructions.
High byte of the indexed load at $5E79. The rectangle routine overwrites it from the current actor slot's page.
Uses the previous rectangle if the actor is off the render area. Otherwise merges the old and new extents, stores the new rectangle for the next pass and continues with the preceding slot.
Resets the twelve bytes at $7520 to $FF and calls the room calculation at $5E51. Marks 28 rectangles inactive, then installs a default rectangle in slot zero.
Scenery plane for depth zero. Its high bit distinguishes the passes that draw it.
Item plane for depth zero. The high nibble selects the item drawing stream.
Cell flags for depth zero, read by the drawing rules and the room transition scripts.
Actor mask at depth zero. Each set bit marks a slot associated with that cell in the expanded actor render window.
Scenery cell codes for depth one. The starting room occupies the window beginning at index $44.
Item plane for depth one. The reward path at $5296 writes six heart values into this page.
Cell flag plane for depth one, installed from the third value of each placement record selecting this depth.
Actor mask for depth one. The initialization path at $5060 records the slot cell when the placement stream sets this mask.
Scenery cell codes for depth two. This group is selected by A equal to 2 at $5095.
Item plane for depth two. Its page number is selected for $BB by the depth 2 path in $5095.
Offset $4E within the depth-two item plane at $6900. This byte is reachable through the indexed depth-plane pointer.
Cell flag plane for depth two, at zero-page pointer $BC/$BD after selecting the group.
Actor plane for depth two, selected through $BE/$BF. Its bits are read by the six-by-six actor scan.
First page of the frame buffer at $6C00–$74FF. $407E supplies this page as the drawing base.
Interleaved flags, tile indices and colour data at offsets $100–$1FF in the active draw buffer. Restored from physical RAM $D100 at $4B73.
Interleaved cell triples at offsets $200–$2FF in the bitmap renderer's working buffer. Copied from physical RAM $D200 at $4B79 before drawing the new frame.
Interleaved cell triples at offsets $300–$3FF in the frame buffer, read by the bitmap blit path. Restored from physical RAM $D300 at $4B7F.
Frame buffer continuation, restored from physical RAM page $D4 by $4B85.
Page restored from physical RAM $D500 by the copy at $4B8B.
Interleaved cell triples at offsets $600–$6FF, also used by the foreground compositing path. Restored from physical RAM $D600 at $4B91.
Interleaved cell triples at offsets $700–$7FF of the 24-row draw buffer. Restored from physical RAM $D700 at $4B97.
Last working-buffer page, copied from physical RAM page $D8 by $4B9D.
Split dispatch addresses indexed by room number from $5DA3.
Inclusive right bounds for the rectangles scanned by the compositor. The compare operand is set to one more than the stored bound.
Starting row coordinate for each rectangle, loaded before selecting the bitmap and cache row addresses.
Inclusive bottom bounds for the rectangle scan. The inner routine patches a limit one greater than this value.
Per-shape offset added while converting the actor cell row to bitmap rows.
Per-shape extent added to the actor's top before clipping the bottom row to 23.
Per-shape offset added to the origin for the actor's left column.
Per-shape value added to the left column before testing the right edge against the drawing area.
Ninety low pointer bytes followed by ninety high bytes, indexed by the shape number from each actor slot in $4223's draw pass.
High byte array of the ninety shape addresses selected by $4223.
Interleaved script addresses in the table identified by the initial player actor record. $5500 uses the index in an actor script to choose its next stream.
Starting script address in the initial position of actor slot zero. The first $3F pairs in this script select native actor handlers.
Low page and high page for three times the cell index, generated at $4B36. Allows a planar cache cell to address its interleaved frame-buffer triple.
Most significant byte of three times the cell index. Generated alongside the low-byte table at $7E00.
Banks the ROMs in, starts menu sound, draws the logo and status panel, and polls input. S starts play. R clears and collects five distinct key definitions before redrawing the menu.
Polls KERNAL GETIN and advances sound while waiting. Returns a seven-bit letter or digit and keeps waiting for other values.
Converts five menu key codes to the corresponding row and column mask bytes for the gameplay poll.
Scans $812A while shifting a column mask and rotating the active-low row mask. Returns after finding the input code or exhausting the rows.
Eight rows of eight key codes. $8106 compares each with the menu key and leaves the matching matrix masks in $816A and $816B.

Converts the remaining-heart count to a collected count by subtracting it from 25. Zeroes the bonus when $0902 differs from one, converts collected, bonus and total to digit codes and draws the resulting score stream.
Converts $091F into two digit-shape codes, patches the heart-count drawing stream at $847F and $8480, then renders stream $0C.
Takes the high nibble of each of the eight slot bytes as a shape selector and draws it at its HUD row.
Repeatedly subtracts ten from A to produce tens in X and units in A. The result is biased for the drawing stream's glyph indices.
Patches the heart-count stream with X and A as its two digit glyphs, then tail-calls the menu stream renderer.
Draws fourteen HUD segments, selecting shape $0A while X is below the current meter value and shape $0B otherwise.
Runs three passes over 42 marked cells. Each pass chooses the next unvisited cell from a pseudorandom starting index and draws a colored logo there.
Uses the low seven bits as a glyph index, with bit 7 advancing to a new line. Patches the source and destination operands and copies eight glyph bytes, then advances the cursor.
Takes the stream number in A and starting cell in X and Y. Interprets zero as end, FF as a new coordinate pair, FE as a color byte, and other bytes as glyph codes.
Reads from the self-modified absolute address, advances it and preserves A as the return value.
Seventeen interleaved pointers. The stream renderer doubles the requested index and copies the selected pointer into the reader's operand.
The first seven drawing streams provide the control-menu key legends and related UI elements.
Stream 7. Used before the inventory slots and meter are drawn on the control screen.
Stream 8, drawn eight times at three-row intervals by the menu.
Stream 9, drawn repeatedly with varied colors in the logo fill.
Stream 10, selected when the drawing loop's index is below $091D.
Stream 11, selected for the remainder of the fourteen meter positions.
Stream 12. The two digit bytes at $847F and $8480 are overwritten before each redraw.
Stream 13, drawn before the game waits for S or R.
Stream 14, used in loops that clear the instruction and score display areas.
Stream 15, patched with the digits for collected hearts, the bonus and their sum.
Stream 16, drawn during initial setup of the menu and HUD.
Returns when the music is disabled or its completion flag is clear. Otherwise reads the next ID from the order table, loops on $7F, stops on a negative value or starts the chosen pattern.
